stories.headline: The Web Learns to Speak Agent: WebMCP Draft Advances Toward W3C Standard
stories.excerpt: A proposal letting websites expose structured tools directly to browser AI agents cleared a key milestone this week, with major browser vendors signaling intent to ship experimental support. Backers argue the spec could replace brittle screen-scraping with consented, auditable agent access to the open web.
stories.licenceBasis: TechCrunch RSS excerpt with link-out, per feed terms of use

stories.headline: OpenSSL Patches Critical Handshake Flaw Scored 9.8 as Agencies Race a Three-Week Deadline
stories.excerpt: CVE-2026-31842, a heap overflow reachable during TLS handshake renegotiation, affects OpenSSL 3.2 through 3.5 and carries a CVSS score of 9.8. Maintainers shipped fixed releases within hours of disclosure; federal agencies have until September 23 to patch under binding operational directives.
stories.licenceBasis: NVD records — U.S. Government work, public domain

stories.headline: Fed Holds at 3.25 Percent, Citing Third Straight Month of Cooling Services Inflation
stories.excerpt: The Federal Open Market Committee left its benchmark rate unchanged at 3.25 percent, noting that services inflation has eased for a third consecutive month while labor markets remain balanced. Two members dissented in favor of a quarter-point cut, the statement shows.
stories.licenceBasis: Federal Reserve press release — U.S. Government work, public domain

stories.headline: Artemis IV Stack Begins Slow Roll to Pad 39B for October Gateway Mission
stories.excerpt: NASA's crawler-transporter carried the fully stacked SLS Block 1B and Orion spacecraft out of the Vehicle Assembly Building overnight, beginning the four-mile journey to Launch Complex 39B. The October window opens the agency's first crewed delivery to the lunar Gateway station.
stories.licenceBasis: NASA media guidelines — U.S. Government work, public domain

stories.headline: Gene-Edited Wheat Endures 40 Percent Less Water Across Three-Year Field Trials
stories.excerpt: Researchers report that CRISPR-edited wheat lines carrying modified stomatal regulators maintained 94 percent of baseline yield under severe irrigation cuts across trial plots in Spain and Australia. The work, published in a peer-reviewed plant science journal, now moves to regulatory review in four countries.
stories.licenceBasis: EurekAlert press release — redistribution with attribution permitted

stories.headline: NOAA Declares La Niña Conditions, Sharpening Forecast for Atlantic Hurricane Peak
stories.excerpt: Sea-surface temperatures in the central Pacific crossed the La Niña threshold in August, NOAA's Climate Prediction Center confirmed, historically a signal of reduced wind shear over the Atlantic basin. Forecasters now put above-normal odds on activity through the season's mid-September peak.
stories.licenceBasis: NOAA text and data — U.S. Government work, public domain

stories.headline: SQLite 3.50 Ships Native Vector Search, and Embedded AI Stacks Take Notice
stories.excerpt: The most deployed database in the world quietly added an approximate-nearest-neighbor index type and distance functions in its latest release, drawing one of the year's largest Hacker News threads. Commenters weigh whether on-device retrieval just became a one-file problem.
stories.licenceBasis: Hacker News public API — titles and links, discussion linked out

stories.headline: Three AI Chip Startups Filed for IPOs in August, EDGAR Records Show
stories.excerpt: An AI-desk review of SEC EDGAR full-text filings found three inference-hardware startups lodged S-1 registration statements within eleven days of each other, together seeking roughly $4.1 billion. All three cite datacenter power constraints as their core market thesis — a pattern, not yet a boom.
stories.licenceBasis: AI synthesis of public-domain EDGAR filings; citations listed

stories.headline: Ransomware Wave Against Regional Hospitals Traces Back to Two Unpatched VPN Flaws
stories.excerpt: Synthesized from vulnerability records: the appliance flaws exploited in August's healthcare ransomware incidents — CVE-2026-27810 and CVE-2026-28455 — were both patched in June and both scored above 9.0. Every disclosed victim ran firmware at least eleven weeks old, the records indicate.
stories.licenceBasis: AI synthesis of public-domain NVD records; citations listed

stories.headline: Deep-Sea Microbes Found Digesting Plastic at Crushing Abyssal Pressures
stories.excerpt: Sediment cores from 6,200 meters down in the Kermadec Trench yielded bacterial strains that metabolize PET at pressures 600 times sea level. The enzymes involved lose activity at surface pressure — a twist that complicates industrial recycling hopes even as it reframes the deep ocean's role in the plastic cycle.
stories.licenceBasis: ScienceDaily release summary with attribution and link-out
